Thanks Elena — good flags. I wanted to capture the MAP checkpoint items so we have a single source of truth going into Thursday’s demo. High-level answers below and a short action table at the end.

Summary (eval plan & acceptance):
- Acceptance surface: functional correctness on 5 representative flows (ingest -> generate -> rerank), latency P50/P95 targets under targeted concurrency, and security controls (KMS integration, token retention policy). The attached evaluation_plan_v1.pdf enumerates the exact test cases and pass/fail criteria.
- Ownership: Redwood will own test execution and remediation for any inference-engine issues; NovaFin will own network and KMS configuration (we’ll provide runbooks). If we encounter an issue in the runtime that requires a patch, Redwood will provide a mitigation build and timeline estimate within 48 hours.
- Contingency: if any critical security gap prevents sign-off we’ll switch the trial to a “grace window” — a two-week extension with focused remediation owners and daily 15-minute standups until resolved.

Blockers called out:
1) KMS handshake intermittency — likely configuration issue (NovaFin) but we’ll add extra verification on our side to isolate client vs. server error.
2) Token/log retention policy clarification for audit logs — NovaFin to share desired retention and legal constraints; we’ll map to Redwood’s retention config and provide options.

Action table (owners & ETA):
- NovaFin: confirm KMS key rotation window and share IAM policy excerpt (owner: Elena) — ETA: Thu 2026-06-25 EOD.
- Redwood: run focused KMS integration test with NovaFin staging keys (owner: Karthik) — ETA: Fri 2026-06-26 midday.
- NovaFin: confirm required token retention window for audit logs (owner: Natalie) — ETA: Thu 2026-06-25.
- Redwood: deliver acceptance_checklist.xlsx (with pass/fail columns) and initial run results (owner: Jonas) — ETA: Thu 2026-06-25 morning.

Can we lock a 30-minute checkpoint Thursday 11:00am PT to review the acceptance checklist and decide go/no-go for the demo? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Jonas

Adding a technical note from our end that may speed diagnostics: when we see intermittent KMS failures in other customers it’s often due to clock skew on the client VM or an intermediate NAT gateway silently resetting TLS sessions. Two quick checks for NovaFin to run:
- Verify the staging VM NTP drift is <3s.
- Confirm any load balancer/NAT idle timeouts are at least 120s during long-lived websocket or streaming sessions.

I’ll run the Redwood-side KMS handshake test against the staging key you sent once we get it (Jonas — I can take point on that). If we see a client-side error code we’ll provide the specific debug trace to help your SREs.

Karthik
